ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-027", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: payments-service: p99 latency above 1000ms for 5 minutes (since 09:43 UTC)
Alerting service: payments
Alert time: 2026-05-20T09:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-20T08:00:00Z to 2026-05-20T11:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-20T10:30:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check latency trend for payments service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-042: Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 209.71 before, 2361.83 after (184.0 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-042] payments.latency_p99_ms from 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z to 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (25 points, 5-minute steps): min=192.66 max=2592.97 mean=1156.64 last=2592.97; mean=1156.64. Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 209.71 before, 2361.83 after (184.0 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-20T09:15:00Z = 192.66 (lowest); 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z = 1008.05 (first point after the change); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 2592.97 (last); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 2592.97 (peak).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-20T10:30:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate trend for payments service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-041: Change detected at 2026-05-20T08:45:00Z: mean 0.28 before, 7.92 after (449.2 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-041] payments.error_rate_pct from 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z to 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (25 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.26 max=15.6 mean=7 last=15.36; mean=7. Change detected at 2026-05-20T08:45:00Z: mean 0.28 before, 7.92 after (449.2 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-20T08:40:00Z = 0.26 (lowest); 2026-05-20T08:45:00Z = 0.44 (first point after the change); 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z = 15.6 (peak); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 15.36 (last).
Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-20T10:30:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check if database connection pool is exhausted for payments service.)
  Result: M-039: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-039] payments.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z to 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (25 points, 5-minute steps): min=21.48 max=36.39 mean=30.06 last=25.16; mean=30.06. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-05-20T09:00:00Z = 21.48 (lowest); 2026-05-20T09:30:00Z = 36.39 (peak); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 25.16 (last).
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-20T10:30:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check if CPU utilization changed during the incident.)
  Result: M-038: Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 38.09 before, 91.73 after (18.3 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-038] payments.cpu_pct from 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z to 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (25 points, 5-minute steps): min=32.89 max=100 mean=61.69 last=99.08; mean=61.69. Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 38.09 before, 91.73 after (18.3 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-20T09:25:00Z = 32.89 (lowest); 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z = 56.13 (first point after the change); 2026-05-20T10:15:00Z = 100 (peak); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 99.08 (last).
Step 5: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-20T10:30:00Z", "metric": "request_rate_rps", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check if there was a traffic spike causing the high latency and error rates.)
  Result: M-044: Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 139.21 before, 584.46 after (94.1 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-044] payments.request_rate_rps from 2026-05-20T08:30:00Z to 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (25 points, 5-minute steps): min=131.41 max=594.2 mean=335.12 last=579.56; mean=335.12. Change detected at 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z: mean 139.21 before, 584.46 after (94.1 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-20T09:25:00Z = 131.41 (lowest); 2026-05-20T09:40:00Z = 576.04 (first point after the change); 2026-05-20T10:15:00Z = 594.2 (peak); 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z = 579.56 (last).
Step 6: log_search {"end": "2026-05-20T09:50:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy, version, error, timeout, slow", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-20T08:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search logs for deployments, errors, or timeouts around the time error rate and latency spiked.)
  Result: 2 matching log lines.
  [L-0299] 2026-05-20T09:43:48Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0310] 2026-05-20T09:48:58Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
Step 7: runbook_retrieve {"query": "how to mitigate and fix traffic spike rate limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding"} (asked because: Retrieve mitigation guidance before diagnosing.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-09-7 (similarity 0.74).
  [R-09-7] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Escalation (similarity 0.74): Call the platform team to raise capacity limits quickly. Tell the business owner about any planned event that nobody mentioned, so capacity can be planned ahead next time. Ask them whether any other region has spare room to take some of the load.
  [R-09-5] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Mitigation (similarity 0.72): Tighten limits on the heaviest caller, raise the ceiling on automatic scaling, and turn away non-essential traffic first. Block abusive sources at the edge. If a client is retrying aggressively, contact whoever owns that client and ask them to back off.
  [R-09-1] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Summary (similarity 0.71): Far more requests are arriving than the service was built to handle. It protects itself by turning some requests away, and capacity cannot grow fast enough to keep up with the demand, so everyone sees slowness or refusals.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: Request volume surged dramatically starting at 09:40 UTC, pushing CPU utilization to 100% and causing severe latency degradation and elevated error rates. (evidence: M-038, M-041, M-042, M-044)
- downstream_timeout: High load and resource saturation from the traffic surge could be causing downstream dependencies to timeout or become unresponsive. (evidence: M-041, M-042, M-044)
- bad_deployment: An initial minor shift in error rate observed earlier at 08:45 UTC could potentially point to a software release or configuration change preceding the load spike. (evidence: M-041)
